$comment: npm-audit equivalent of .trivyignore, consumed by scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs (the blocking Security Scan step). Every entry needs an advisory id, the tree it applies to (scope = npm prefix, or '*'), a reason, an added date, and an expires date. 🔴 expires is ENFORCED as of 2026-08-28: past its date the entry stops suppressing and the advisory blocks again, because a review cadence written only in prose is how a suppression list becomes permanent. Expiring does not mean the advisory is fixed — it means a human undertook to look again by then. Re-justify with a new date, or remove the entry.

exceptions.reason: image-size ICNS-parser DoS. npm reports the vulnerable range as '*' — EVERY published version is affected, so there is no version to upgrade to (1.2.1 is the last of the 1.x line, published the same day upstream moved to 2.0.2, and 2.x is not fixed either). npm's only offered 'fix' is react-native 0.72.17, flagged isSemVerMajor — a major DOWNGRADE from 0.81.5 that would break the app without fixing the flaw. Reachable only via metro, the Expo/React-Native dev bundler (@expo/metro, @react-native/community-cli-plugin): it reads image dimensions while building the JS bundle on a developer machine or CI runner, does not ship in the compiled APK/IPA, and never runs on a server. The images it parses are the repo's own committed assets, not untrusted input. Same reachability class as the undici/ws and image-size CVE entries in .trivyignore. Remove as soon as upstream publishes a fixed image-size that metro accepts.

image-size JXL/HEIF-parser DoS — same package, same vulnerable range '*', same dev-bundler-only reachability and same absent fix as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr above; see that entry for the full reasoning. Remove both together when a fixed image-size ships.

node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements (CVE-2026-85393). Affected range <= 1.4.0, first_patched_version NONE, and 1.4.0 is the latest release, so there is no version to upgrade to. Reachable only through developer tooling: @expo/cli (src/utils/codesigning.js, src/run/ios/codeSigning/Security.js) and expo-updates' `codesigning:*` CLI (cli/build/*CodeSigningAsync.js) — expo-updates' runtime entry build/index.js does not import it, no mobile app source imports node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates, and app.json configures no update code signing, so nothing in the shipped APK/IPA verifies a signature with it. Short expiry on purpose: re-check for a fixed node-forge then. Mirrored in .trivyignore.

braces stack-exhaustion DoS through deeply nested patterns (CVE-2026-93687), first reported 2026-10-03. braces 3.0.3 is the latest release and no fixed version exists. npm counts it as a production dependency only because metro's file map (metro-file-map, jest-haste-map, @jest/transform) lists micromatch -> braces as a dependency; metro is the Expo/React-Native dev bundler and runs on a developer machine or CI runner, never in the shipped app. No mobile app source imports braces or micromatch, so neither is in the APK/IPA bundle, and the patterns it expands are the repo's own globs, not untrusted input. Same reachability class as the image-size entries above. Short expiry on purpose: re-check for a fixed braces then. Mirrored in .trivyignore (CVE-2026-93687).

braces stack-exhaustion DoS (CVE-2026-93687); braces 3.0.3 is the latest release and no fixed version exists. In web-uk it arrives via chokidar 3.6.0, from nodemon and sass (devDependencies) and from nunjucks's OPTIONAL chokidar peer — so it IS installed in the production image, but never executed there: nunjucks require()s chokidar only when its `watch` option is on (node_modules/nunjucks/src/node-loaders.js), and web-uk/src/server.js sets `watch: NODE_ENV === 'development'`, while the production image (web-uk/Dockerfile) and compose.webuk.bluegreen.yml run with NODE_ENV=production. Even in development chokidar only expands the repo's own template paths, never request input. Short expiry on purpose: re-check for a fixed braces then. Mirrored in .trivyignore (CVE-2026-93687).
